skill.name: git-commit
skill.description: Guide for breaking changes into logical, atomic commits using interactive staging. Use when committing changes that span multiple concerns, when needing to stage parts of files (hunks), when asked to create well-organized commit history, or when changes should be split into multiple commits.
skill.summary: Organizes mixed Git changes into logical, atomic commits with interactive staging guidance.
skill.author: Chemiseblanc

content.user_title: Organize Git Changes into Atomic Commits
content.value_statement: Mixed changes make review, rollback, and release notes harder. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused Git commits.
actual_capabilities: Reviews staged and unstaged changes before commit planning.
Separates unrelated work into logical commit groups.
Guides whole-file staging and partial hunk staging.
Checks the staged diff before each commit.
Uses a separate commit-message skill for message formatting.
limitations: Requires a Git repository with accessible working tree status.
Does not run tests or validate application behavior by itself.
Does not resolve merge conflicts or rewrite published history.
Needs user approval or tool execution to create commits.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Mixed Local Changes
use_cases.description: Separate feature work, bug fixes, and formatting into commits that reviewers can inspect independently.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Reviewable Pull Request
use_cases.description: Build a clear commit history before opening a pull request or responding to review feedback.

use_cases.title: Split Risky Refactors
use_cases.description: Keep file moves, refactors, and behavior changes in separate commits for safer review and rollback.

prompt_templates.title: Group My Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize my current Git changes into logical commits. Show the proposed commit groups before staging anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for understanding a mixed working tree.

prompt_templates.title: Stage the First Commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review staged and unstaged changes, suggest commit groups, then stage only the first safe group.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for starting a clean commit series.

prompt_templates.title: Separate Mixed Hunks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use partial staging to separate unrelated changes in the same file, then verify the staged diff.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow when one file contains multiple concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Review-Ready Series
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a complete commit sequence for this branch, create each focused commit, and stop before any risky history rewrite.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for preparing a polished pull request.

output_examples.input: A branch contains a bug fix, a formatting cleanup, and documentation edits.
output: Proposes three commit groups by purpose.
Stages the bug fix first with its related test.
Leaves formatting and documentation for later commits.

output_examples.input: One source file contains a refactor and new validation behavior.
output: Identifies the unrelated changes in the same file.
Uses partial staging to isolate the refactor.
Reviews the staged diff before preparing the commit.

output_examples.input: A maintainer wants a pull request history that is easier to review.
output: Separates file moves from behavior changes.
Keeps each commit focused on one reversible concern.
Checks remaining changes after every commit.

best_practices: Review the staged diff before each commit.
Keep each commit focused on one logical concern.
Pair bug fixes with their related tests when possible.
anti_patterns: Committing unrelated features, fixes, and formatting together.
Using partial staging without checking the staged result.
Mixing file moves with behavior changes in one commit.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: It provides a workflow for staging and committing. Actual commits require tool execution and user approval in supported environments.

faq.question: Can it handle changes inside one file?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides partial staging so unrelated hunks in one file can become separate commits.

faq.question: Does it write commit messages?
faq.answer: It references a separate commit-message skill for formatting. This skill focuses on grouping and staging changes.

faq.question: Is it useful for pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps create a commit history that reviewers can follow and maintainers can revert safely.

faq.question: Does it run tests before committing?
faq.answer: No. Test execution is outside the documented workflow and should be requested separately.

faq.question: Can it rewrite Git history?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow organizes current working tree changes and does not instruct rebasing or force pushing.
